note: Written before any risky candidate is run. A size is read from the README, a HEAD request or the Google Drive page; 'not found' means it was not found out.

candidates.reason: The README gives no download command or address: MNIST and the other data sets are fetched implicitly by the training library, which is not an address named in the README.

The data is named (Google Drive: graph file about 2 MB, data file about 111 MB, sizes read from the Drive pages), but the README command is 'python sdcn.py --name [usps|hhar|reut|acm|dblp|cite]': a list of alternatives, not one concrete value. The protocol does not choose values (section 2), so the command is not run.

The README commands use a variable ('--config ./configs/tourism/$landmark.json'), not a concrete value, and the data (image-matching-challenge images and a Google Drive folder of poses) has no size that was found out. Not run.

The data for the listed command (--test_dataset CropDisease) is fetched with the Kaggle command line ('kaggle datasets download -d plant-disease/data'), which needs an account; miniImageNet and the models are Dropbox links of unknown size.
The data is one Google Drive file of 5.3 GB (size read from the Drive page), above the 3 GB limit for a single file; the README command is also 'python main.py <model>' (a placeholder).
The README says the CIFAR data is downloaded automatically by torchvision; it names no address or command that fetches it.

The data sets (enron, facebook, colab) are files of the repository itself (datasets/raw_data/), so there is nothing to download (0 GB). The README command 'python main.py --dataset_name enron' is concrete (README, Running the Code).
The README names no data address: the GLUE data and the model weights are fetched implicitly from Hugging Face.
The data is a mega.nz link; no download tool for mega.nz is available on this machine and its size was not found out.

The listed command needs an earlier step of the README (save_pca_and_ica_embeddings.py) and files under output/ in the repository (read-only in the sandbox), GloVe (822 MB, nlp.stanford.edu) and a downloaded and compiled LKH solver; compiling third-party code is not an allowed repair.
The README says the data sets are downloaded automatically and refers to DATASETS.md for broken links; it names no address or command for the data of the listed command.
